headline: Continued review of plan to replace fallen brick with vinyl siding at 38 Main St to December 9th; approved September 9, 2026 minutes.
summary: Members said they had no concerns with plans to replace a few slate roof tiles at 24 West Allen St. For 38 Main St, they asked the applicant for other siding materials, a mock-up on the building, and cost figures. Staff also gave updates on the Comprehensive Plan and a historic district survey.
decisions: Approved the September 9, 2026 meeting minutes unanimously.
Continued the Certificate of Appropriateness application for 38 Main St to the December 9th meeting.

decision_titles: Certificate of Appropriateness application for 38 Main St
plain_text:
11/18/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: Britta Tonn, Chair; Doug Johnson; Sue O’Brien; Maggie Hicks
City Staff Present: Ravi Venkataraman, Director of City Planning
Guests Present: Steve Guild
Call to Order by: Britta
Meeting Start Time: 6:02 pm
Minutes Recorded by: Ravi
Changes to the Agenda
None
Public Comment
None
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by Doug, seconded by Maggie, to approve the September 9, 2026 meeting minutes. 
Voting: unanimous. Motion carried.
Discussion: 24 West Allen St
Ravi said that the applicant is looking to replace a few slate tiles on the roof, adding that a zoning 
permit would not be required for the maintenance work because the scope of work is limited, 
and that he thought the board should be notified of the minor maintenance work on the historic 
property. The board expressed their appreciation in the church’s work in maintaining the historic 
nature of the building, and said that they had no concerns with the approach of the proposed 
maintenance. The board suggested that the applicant work with a slate roof specialist for the 
maintenance work.
Certificate of Appropriateness Application: 38 Main St
Steve Guild gave an overview of the proposed work, stating that the property owner is looking to 
replace the fallen brick on the southerly side of the building with vinyl siding. Maggie asked for 
clarification on the existing conditions and for the cause of the bricks falling. Steve said that the 
clips holding up the brick gave away. Britta said that the Google street view shows the existing 
conditions of the building and the conditions of the building before the bricks fell. Ravi presented 
the Google street view of the building presently and in the past. Ravi asked Steve for the cost 
difference between vinyl and brick. Britta said she would appreciate seeing an exact number. 
Steve said that brick would be double the cost compared to vinyl. Maggie said that the vinyl 
siding in the mock up doesn’t appear consistent with the existing brick on the street-facing 
façade, and suggested vinyl brick veneer or other alternatives that would look like brick.
Britta and Maggie pointed out the distinctive ornamentals around the lintels of the windows. The 
board concurred in retaining those elements around the windows. Britta discussed the 
environmental impacts of vinyl and suggested more durable alternatives, like wood and hardie 
board. Maggie agreed, adding that vinyl could trap more moisture and cause more damage in 
the long term. Sue pointed out the importance of the building in the City, the details of the 
building in the state historic register photo, and the need to repoint the bricks currently on the 
building.
Ravi summarized the board’s requests to the applicant—to see other alternatives for materials 
for the siding, to see the mock up of these materials on the building and to review the costs of 
the materials. Ravi reviewed the meeting calendar and asked for the board’s availability in 
December. The board reviewed possible dates and concluded that a quorum is more likely to be 
available on December 9th. The board came to consensus to continue the item to the 
December 9th meeting to review the additional requests to the applicant.
City Updates
Ravi said that the Planning Commission is working on the Comprehensive Plan update, and that 
he does not have many permit applications on his desk currently.
Other Business
Britta discussed the work on the Winooski Falls Historic District survey as part of the Burlington-
Winooski Bridge project, and said that public engagement on the survey work is forthcoming.
Sue gave an update on the historic plaque project, and said that she will be taking a break on 
this project until the spring.
Adjourn
Motion by: Doug
Second: Maggie
Meeting End Time: 6:52 pm

VIII.
IX.
DRAFT
